pointers.sentence: It sends a site's cookies with the requests that other sites' pages make it send, as far as each cookie's SameSite attribute allows, so a page elsewhere may post a form to this site with the user's credentials: the attack the documentation calls a **cross-site request forgery** (`docs/ref/csrf.txt`).

The harbour office's site, which takes requests for berths at harbour.example, installs the four in the order `SecurityMiddleware`, `CsrfViewMiddleware`, `XFrameOptionsMiddleware`, `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware`; it requires HTTPS (`SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`, with `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS` of an hour) and sets a content security policy whose scripts must come from the site itself or carry the request's **nonce**, a random value that the policy names and an inline script repeats (`SECURE_CSP`, with `CSP.SELF` and `CSP.NONCE`) (`django/utils/csp.py:CSP`).

By the way out the template has made the secret and the nonce that the way in left unmade, and each middleware has something to write (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_request`, `django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_request`).

By the way out the template has made the secret and the nonce that the way in left unmade, and each middleware has something to write (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_request`, `django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_request`).

After Content-Type, which the response was made with, the headers stand in the order the middleware added them, and the cookie comes last, since a response keeps its cookies apart from its headers and the handler writes them after (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).

Over plain HTTP the same request goes no further than the first layer, which answers it with a redirect to HTTPS ([The security headers: `SecurityMiddleware` and `XFrameOptionsMiddleware`](security/headers.md)) (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).

So `CsrfViewMiddleware` keeps a CSRF secret for a browser, in its cookie or, with `CSRF_USE_SESSIONS`, in the session, and the site's own pages carry a token made from it, a different one on every page ([The CSRF secret and its token](security/csrf-token.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:get_token`).

Before the view, a request of a method that is not **safe**, as `"GET"`, `"HEAD"`, `"OPTIONS"` and `"TRACE"` are, must ordinarily come from the site's own origin or a trusted one and carry a token that matches the browser's secret; one that fails is answered by the failure view, with a 403 by default, in place of its view ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](security/csrf-check.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).

None of them replaces a header the response already has ([The security headers: `SecurityMiddleware` and `XFrameOptionsMiddleware`](security/headers.md)) (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`, `django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response`, `django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response`).

The nonce `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_request` gives each request is a `LazyNonce`, made only when something first reads it, so on the way out `build_policy` writes it into the policy if it was made and leaves it out if not ([Content Security Policy and the nonce](security/csp.md)) (`django/utils/csp.py:build_policy`).

Django makes its values with `SECRET_KEY` alone, and its signers, the password-reset tokens and `get_user`, reading back the hash a session keeps, check what comes back against it and then against each of `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, which is how a site changes its key without at once refusing everything made with the old one ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](security/keys.md)) (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`, `django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`).

The value `dumps` signs is only encoded, in base64 and sometimes compressed, which anyone can undo: a signature makes a change detectable and hides nothing ([Signing: `Signer`, `TimestampSigner`, `dumps` and `loads`](security/signing.md)) (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`).
